facts.statement: The genus Acanthopleurus was described by Agassiz in 1844.
The genus contains three species: A. collettei, A. serratus, and A. trispinosus.
facts.quote: subdivision: * †A. collettei Tyler, 1980 †A. serratus Agassiz, 1844 †A. trispinosus (Ciobanu, 1977)

facts.statement: Acanthopleurus was an extinct marine fish that lived in the seas over modern-day Europe during the early Oligocene epoch.
facts.quote: Acanthopleurus is an extinct genus of marine triplespine that lived in the seas over what is now Europe during the early Oligocene epoch.

facts.statement: The species A. collettei lived in the Oligocene of Switzerland within the Matt Formation.
facts.quote: †A. collettei Tyler, 1980 - Oligocene of Switzerland (Matt Formation)

facts.statement: The type species A. serratus lived in the Oligocene of Switzerland within the Matt Formation.
facts.quote: †A. serratus Agassiz, 1844 - Oligocene of Switzerland (Matt Formation) (type species)

facts.statement: The species A. trispinosus lived in the Oligocene of Romania.
facts.quote: †A. trispinosus (Ciobanu, 1977) - Oligocene of Romania (=Cephalacanthus trispinosus Ciobanu, 1977)

facts.statement: The former species A. brevis is now classified in the separate genus Cryptobalistes.
facts.quote: The former species A. brevis Rath, 1859 is now classified in its own genus, Cryptobalistes.

facts.statement: Acanthopleurus is classified in the kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Actinopterygii, order Tetraodontiformes, and family Xenacanthidae.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Actinopterygii ordo: Tetraodontiformes familia: Xenacanthidae genus: Acanthopleurus

facts.statement: Acanthopleurus was described by Agassiz in 1843.
Acanthopleurus is an extinct genus of prehistoric ray-finned fish.
facts.quote: Acanthopleurus es un género extinto de peces actinopterigios prehistóricos.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Acanthopleurus is Xenacanthidae.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Acanthopleurus in the class Chondrichthyes.
